where: mac4DSTEM/UI/InspectorRows.swift:749 (shown), :755 (blur commits), :760 (.onDisappear(perform: commit)), :782-789 (commit), :796-802 (resolve; the only guard is `parsed != current` at :800)
mechanism:
The field's text is always the FORMATTED value (`shown`, :749). commit() runs on blur (:755), on Return, and on .onDisappear (:760) even if nothing was typed. It feeds the shown text to resolve(), which parses it and calls onCommit whenever the parse differs from the stored value (:800). So whenever the format shows fewer digits than the stored value has, merely focusing and leaving the field, or leaving the room or closing the sheet, silently stores the ROUNDED value. A typed 0.0125 into a 3-digit field is stored exactly, then rounded to 0.013 at the next blur or room switch. Float-backed rows (disk-detection params via doubleBinding) also re-commit every time, because Double(Float 0.3) != 0.3. Each such write fires diskParams.didSet -> onParamsChange (live overlay re-detect, DiskDetectionProduct.swift:56). Setters with change-guards then invalidate results. Q/R scale fields are the exception: they already have a tolerance patch (AppState+Open.swift:1416, 5e-7) and show 0...6 digits, so Q 0.0275 is NOT shown as 0,03 and is safe. PhaseMappingSettings.displayFormat (:690) is a second partial patch (min...6 digits).

AFFECTED FIELDS (shown precision vs real precision):
(1) Ptychography Defocus, 0...1 digit (ReconstructionSettings.swift:167-171), and Astigmatism C12a/C12b, 0...1 (:223-236). Both are seeded by 'Use Parallax Fit' from the fit's full-precision Doubles (PtychographySettings.swift:65-69). They round to 0.1 A, up to 0.05 A off, after the first blur or room switch. The seed status line prints the unrounded %g value. This is the one that matters scientifically.
(2) Manual ellipse a, b, 0...4, and theta in degrees, 0...3 (PrepareSettings.swift:425-455). The drafts start from the fit's full-precision values (a, b to 1e-4 px; theta to 1e-3 deg = 1.7e-5 rad). Effect on b/a is about 1e-6 relative.
(3) Ellipse fit annulus inner/outer, 0...2 (PrepareSettings.swift:337-350). Defaults are 0.35 and 0.9 times half the detector (AppState+Open.swift:483), e.g. 44.625 -> 44.63. Effect is under 0.01 px.
(4) Learned threshold, 2 digits (MapSettings.swift:288-291): typed 0.555 is stored as 0.56 after a blur or room switch.
(5) AdjustmentSlider rows with an unstepped Slider and fewer digits than the slider produces: Exploratory scale, 4 digits, range 0.001...0.05 (MapSettings.swift:1237-1243). Its didSet calls invalidateResult() on any change, so leaving the room after dragging DISCARDS the ACOM result. Also Gamma 2 digits (PaneOverlays.swift:397,411; display only) and the region Radius, 0 digits (ImagingSettings.swift:98-107, an integer-rounded radius after a fractional drag).
(6) Excitation slab, fixed 3 digits (PhaseMappingSettings.swift:616-626).
(7) Min. absolute intensity, 1...5 significant digits (MapSettings.swift:593-598); relative intensity %, 0...3 (:603).
(8) Voltage and hot-pixel threshold, 0...2 (PrepareSettings.swift:162-166; PreprocessSheet.swift:161-163). A file voltage with more than 2 digits is rounded, and any change calls invalidatePlan() (AppState+Open.swift:1504).
(9) Parallax and depth fields at 0...3/0...4/0...1/0...2 digits (ReconstructionSettings.swift:402-531), whose values replay can restore at full precision (ResultExport.swift:929-945).
Not affected: integer fields, and the Q/R scale fields (patched).
fix: Fix once, in resolve(): before parsing, return .keep when the trimmed typed text equals the shown text of the current value (`if let current, typed == entry.format(current) { return .keep }`). An unedited field then never commits, wherever its format rounds. A typed text that differs from the shown text still parses and commits as today. Then delete the two compensating patches as dead weight: AppState.isUnchangedManualScale (+ its two call sites at AppState+Open.swift:1422, :1464) and the 'minimum...6' reasoning in PhaseMappingSettings.displayFormat. Keep the Q/R tolerance if you want belt and braces. Known caveat: typing exactly the displayed text (e.g. '0,03' while 0.0275 is stored) is a no-op; typing '0.03' or '0,030' still sets it. Optional extension: show the full-precision text while the field has focus.

Reproduce on screen first (Use Parallax Fit, then switch rooms, read Defocus and the provenance). Run an independent refuter on the diagnosis. where: mac4DSTEM/Core/Data/DM4Reader.swift:93-96 (Data(contentsOf:options:)), :130-134 (readingOptions: MNT_LOCAL -> .alwaysMapped, else .mappedIfSafe), :422-441 (decode withUnsafeBytes), :209-260 (scanFastestGather withUnsafeBytes); reads at :315 readPattern, :325 readScanRow, :370 readScanTile; self-documented at :117-119; docs/open-items.md:211-212; no handler anywhere (grep didUnmount/willUnmount/volumeIsRemovable/isRemovable/SIGBUS handlers: no hits in mac4DSTEM/; only NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting at App/mac4DSTEMApp.swift:11 and the doc-comments above)
mechanism:
Confirmed by reading, not reproduced here (no volume was unplugged). ONLY the DM4/DM3 reader maps a file, on any MNT_LOCAL volume including an external SSD: DM4Reader holds `private let data: Data` (:57) from init until the dataset is released. Every other reader goes through calls that return errors: HDF5 uses H5Fopen with the default property list (no mmap driver; H5Dread status < 0 becomes H5Error.readFailed, H5Reader.swift:511-512); EMPAD/MIB use FileHandle seek+read (VendorRawReaders.swift:210-217, throws); VendorRawReaders.swift:152 maps only the small EMPAD .xml at open. What touches the mapping: decode() and scanFastestGather() on the actor, called from readPattern (pattern browser, DatasetPreview.swift:187, PendingLoad.swift:250, OriginCalibration.swift:707, DetectorFineTuning), readScanRow and readScanTile (the load tile loop, imaging). If the volume has vanished, a page not already in the page cache faults, the kernel delivers SIGBUS, and Swift has no way to catch it: the app dies with no dialog. The existing truncation guards (`start + need <= data.count`, :429) check the mapping's length, not the volume. Exposure is narrower than the open-items line implies: while idle nothing touches the mapping, and once the cube is resident FourDArray.pattern() slices RAM (FourDArray.swift ~:21-32), so the crash needs a read of a NON-resident dataset or a load in flight. DM4 on a network volume (not MNT_LOCAL) is read whole into RAM (.mappedIfSafe), so no SIGBUS there (a separate RAM problem, already noted at :121-124). macOS eject: a normal Finder eject of a volume with a mapped file normally refuses (file in use); a cable yank, Force Eject, or a USB disk dropped at sleep does not (from macOS behaviour I know; not tested here). Reproduction recipe exists for a session: tools/dm4-parity-probe already uses an exFAT disk image (docs/archive/v4/almgsi-gateD-2026-09-24.md part 8); `hdiutil attach`, open the DM4, `hdiutil detach -force`, then read a pattern.

Options assessed. (a) NSWorkspace willUnmount/didUnmount observer: willUnmount is NOT posted for a yank, and didUnmount arrives on the main thread after the fact, so it loses the race to an in-flight tile (seconds from a slow disk); it needs an owner (observer token cannot go in AppState; DatasetSession would host it) plus a reader-side revoked flag anyway; and closing the dataset would throw away a resident cube that is still valid. As a message it is nice, as the safety it is not enough. (b) read()/pread instead of mapping: reliable (EIO thrown, a real error dialog) but DM4Reader is built on the mapping: ByteReader parses the header tag tree by random access (:823-885), and the scan-fastest gather exists because mapping makes 215,040 strided touches cost 0.04 s (comment at :200-208 measured 3.7 s -> 0.04 s on Si-SiGe.dm4); a read-the-file rule is what the owner retired on 2026-09-24 (28 GB on an 8 GB Mac). Large rewrite, perf and RAM risk. (c) say it in Known limitations: CHANGELOG v4.1.0 'Known limitations' (CHANGELOG.md:84-97) does not mention it today. (d, rejected) a SIGBUS handler with sigsetjmp/siglongjmp: Swift cannot do it and it would need a C shim, against the pure-Swift bar.
fix: Recommended: (c) now plus a small reader-side guard. Guard: in DM4Reader capture the volume identity at init (statfs f_fsid of the path, or stat st_dev) and run a `try requireVolumeAlive()` at the top of readPattern, readScanRow, readScanTile (not per decode; one statfs is ~microseconds against a multi-ms tile), throwing a new `DM4Error.volumeGone(name)` with errorDescription like '<file> is no longer reachable: its disk was disconnected. Loaded data stays open; reconnect the disk and reopen the file to read more.' The error already travels the existing try/await chain to alerts. This covers the common case (disk pulled while idle or between tiles) and still leaves a window of one tile / a few ms between check and touch; say so in the Known limitations line. Only apply the guard when readingOptions returned .alwaysMapped (local volume). Add the one-line known limitation to CHANGELOG v4.1.0 regardless: 'A disk pulled out while a DM4 is being read can still crash the app mid-read; the app refuses the next read with a message.' Do NOT build (a) or (b) in the plateau.
effort: Guard + error case + test: S (about 30 lines and one test, 1-2 h incl. the hdiutil force-detach drive on a scratch build). Known-limitations line alone: XS. Option (a) on top: M. Option (b): L.
decision_options: 1) Guard + Known limitations line (recommended): S effort, low risk (reads only, no number moves); closes the idle-unplug crash, residual in-flight-tile race documented; loaded/resident work keeps going. 2) Known limitations line only: XS, zero code risk, the crash stays and the app loses the open session on yank mid-read (and a save may be lost, the sidecar session file lives beside the dataset). 3) Guard + didUnmount status message (also text 'Disk X was disconnected; loaded data is still in memory'): M, new owner for an observer in DatasetSession, adds a status line, still does not stop the in-flight race; only worth it if he wants the proactive message. 4) pread-based DM4 reader for external volumes: L, real fix for the race, but slower scan-fastest and header parsing rewrite, conflicts with the retired read-the-file rule; not for v4.1.
test_hint: Unit (DSTEMCore, next to DM4ReadingOptionsTests): build a tiny synthetic DM4 in NSTemporaryDirectory, open DM4Reader, unlink the file (or point the stored identity at a path whose statfs fails) and assert readPattern/readScanTile throw DM4Error.volumeGone instead of returning pixels; break it by removing the guard call and watch the read succeed on the unlinked mapping. The real SIGBUS is not unit-testable: drive it once with an exFAT/APFS disk image and `hdiutil detach -force` on a scratch build, pid-pinned, per the repo's drive rule; before the guard the process must die, after it show the error.
